edits.new:
### A.7 Mechanical

- **r7 outline (round 4, H.23(a)).** The **r7 outline** is the r6 rectangle x 17.70-48.70, y 34.14-67.14 plus two tabs, with the
  pin-11 chamfer relocated. **Tab X** is the CR extension toward the Teensy, x 48.70-65.00, y 56.30-68.30 (195.60 mm²). **Tab Y**
  is the CR extension toward L-FC, x 17.70-37.56, y 67.14-76.00 (175.96 mm²). The gross area is 1394.06 mm² (r6 rectangle 1023.00
  + tab X 195.60 + tab Y 175.96 - chamfer 0.50 mm²); the bounding box is x 17.70-65.00, y 34.14-76.00 = 47.30 x 41.86 mm. The
  following table lists the vertices in board coordinates (A.8 convention), counter-clockwise from the -x/-y corner.

| Vertex | x | y | Corner |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | 17.70 | 34.14 | convex |
| V2 | 48.70 | 34.14 | convex |
| V3 | 48.70 | 56.30 | concave |
| V4 | 65.00 | 56.30 | convex |
| V5 | 65.00 | 68.30 | convex |
| V6 | 48.70 | 68.30 | convex |
| V7 | 48.70 | 67.14 | concave |
| V8 | 37.56 | 67.14 | concave |
| V9 | 37.56 | 76.00 | convex |
| V10 | 18.70 | 76.00 | convex (chamfer end) |
| V11 | 17.70 | 75.00 | convex (chamfer end) |

- **Concave corners (r7):** V3 (48.70, 56.30), V7 (48.70, 67.14) and V8 (37.56, 67.14) are the tab-root inside corners. The
  router leaves a fillet of its minimum inside-corner radius in each of them, TODO(verify: MS8 minimum inside-corner radius);
  T-A-06 checks the courtyard inset and the bottom clearance rule on the filleted outline.
- **Tab content (r7; per-region rules in A.8).** Tab X carries on its top the tap field (20 SMT pads on a 6 x 4 grid at 2.54 mm,
  x 50.80-63.50, y 58.94-66.56), R175 and two spare grid positions; on its bottom, thermal-band-class passives under the bottom
  clearance rule; and FT1. Tab Y carries on its top the LVC gates U105-U110, U114, U116 and U118 with their decouplers; on its
  bottom, logic pull-downs, series resistors and decouplers; and FT2 with its fill hole. The residual tap pads F08 (T22), F09
  (T8), F10 (T9) and F22 (T18) stay on the footprint low row y 35.80, and the rest of the freed r6 tap-field area becomes the
  comparator region (A.8). The straight-length sum of the 20 taps falls from 1308.0 mm to 850.9 mm (-34.9 %; 856.7 mm dressed,
  H.23(g)). Tap wires from tab X are dressed toward +y until x > 63, never over the LM1084 body (A.4). W5 leaves J101 toward +y
  and crosses tab X at its fold height with W1/W2, clear of the tap pads (A.3). The CR ends of W1-W4, the W6/W7 pads and the
  J101 region are unchanged.
- **Tab trims and neighbours (r7, H.23(b)).** No MB part box overlaps either tab. Tab Y ends at x 37.56 so that ROP1-FC (box
  0.501 mm from the tab) and ROP2-FC (1.664 mm) stay uncovered and reachable: they set the OPA197 gain of the FC droop network,
  whose AD5443/OPA197 DMM block measurement is an open bench item. OP-FC lies 2.659 mm from tab Y. Tab Y ends at y 76.00 so that
  the L-FC body keeps 0.862 mm with the Eaton 12.9 mm body centred on its footprint origin (ASSUMPTION, TODO(verify: Eaton
  HCM1A1305V3 drawing), MS3 caliper) and 1.012 mm with the 12.6 mm silkscreen body; at y 76.51 these would be 0.352 / 0.502 mm.
  The tab X neighbours are MDAC-FC (box 1.701 mm from the top edge), REG-5V (box 1.786 mm, body 3.953 mm from the low edge) and
  C-D2 (box 2.181 mm from the right edge). The tab Y neighbours are J-FC (box 0.470 mm, body 1.570 mm from the chamfer) and
  J-NTC (1.448 mm). Neither tab covers a named rework point: the R171/T2 joint on C-D2 pad 1 lies 3.118 mm from tab X, ROP1-FC
  and ROP2-FC 0.501 and 1.664 mm from tab Y, and RENC2, BAL pad 8, RB1A, CBL2, CO-5V and the T18 point >= 14.318 mm from both.
- **Clearances on copper rims (r7, H.23(b)).** Every plan clearance to MB copper is computed on the copper rim: a trace by half
  its width, a polygon by half its outline width beyond its vertex path, a via by its 0.7564 mm pad and an MB CHG header pad by its
  1.650 mm square. The VBUS L1 polygon (outline width 1.016 mm) reaches 0.024 mm from the tab X right edge x 65.00, and the
  MPPT-DISABLE via pad at (65.024, 61.722) reaches 0.354 mm over it. The 5V via pad at (59.389, 55.579) and the 5V L1 trace rim
  lie 0.343 mm and 0.467 mm below the tab X low edge. These rims bear on nothing, because the tab underside carries no exposed
  copper over them (bottom clearance rule, L4 solder mask, polyimide sheet).
- **Rejected extension zones (r7; `round4/work/mb_mechanical.md` sections 3 and 6.4).** The -x zone and the zone past x = 0 lie
  over or beside J-BL/J-FC (21.70 mm) and J-NTC (13.90 mm), whose wire entries and screws must stay reachable. The -y zone covers
  the rework points BAL pad 8 (T22, PM11), RB1A and CBL2 and lies 2.96 mm from VSW-BT. Wide or edge-reaching +y zones need a
  raised stack and cover the FC droop analog or a boost switching node. An extension past x 65.00 is a 34.2 mm cantilever (first
  mode estimated at 0.51-0.73 kHz) over 139 mm² of the 16 V VBUS pour, with its tip 0.5 mm from RENC2 in the unrecorded
  encoder-bodge area. Mounting the EVM on the CR covers the whole FC boost channel, which has an open undiagnosed fault.
- **Outline freeze (r7):** the tab outlines are frozen only after the T-A-08 survey passes (MS3: unrecorded items inside each tab
  outline + 0.5 mm and under each foot spot, L-FC body by caliper). A fail trims the tab and re-runs `round4/calc/r7_calc.py`.
- **Pin-11 chamfer (r7, relocated):** the 1.0 mm x 45 degree chamfer moves to the tab Y -x/+y corner (17.70, 76.00), edge
  (18.70, 76.00)-(17.70, 75.00). It stays the only chamfered corner and marks the pin-11 side on the CR, on the polyimide sheet
  print and on the T-A-06 1:1 print. The r6 chamfer corner (17.70, 67.14) is now a point on the straight left edge x 17.70. A
  y-mirrored capture moves the chamfer to a low-y corner and puts tab X over REG-5V (4.83 mm tall), so the mirrored CR cannot
  seat; the print check (T-A-06 step 0) still catches the mirror before ordering. The pads are unchanged, so
  `calc/pin_identity_check.py` is unchanged.
- **Header stack (r7, unchanged from r6; H.23(j)).** The strips stay Samtec TSW-110-07-G-S (column x 45.998, pins 1-10) and
  TSW-112-07-G-S (column x 20.998, pins 11-22): 2.54 mm PBT body, 0.64 mm square post, no spacer and no raised stack. The body
  seats on the 0.125 mm polyimide sheet, so the CR underside is 2.665 mm and the CR top 4.265 mm above the MB top (CR 1.6 mm,
  TODO(verify: CR fab stack-up); MB 1.6 mm, TODO(measure: MS6 caliper at the CHG holes)). The r6 PM4 orientation stays (short end
  B up through the CR, long end C down through the MB; Samtec F-226: A 10.92, B 2.54, C 5.84 mm): CR-top protrusion 0.940 mm,
  MB-bottom protrusion 4.115 mm before the PM4 step-4 cut. The W5 IDC socket and ribbon fold (>= 8.0 mm above the CR top, A.3)
  stay the tallest item: the stack top is >= 12.265 mm plus the cable thickness (TODO(verify: cable assembly drawing)) against the
  nominal Ag105 envelope of 13.14 mm (`AG105_Silvertel.pdf` Figure 11 p.21), a margin of <= 0.875 mm before the cable. Gate D-2
  (MS1: the measured Ag105 standoff and module top height; `docs/reviews/battery_isolation_2026-11-07/detailed_design_IC1.md`
  section 15.2) decides before PM1. The tabs and feet add no height: the header bodies set the CR height.
- CR outline 31.0 x 33.0 mm stays inside the CHG silkscreen (32.0 x 34.8 mm) (**superseded in r7:** the r6 rectangle is now the
  footprint part of the r7 outline, and tab X and tab Y extend the CR past the silkscreen; the header-body statement below
  stands).

edits.old: C-DC11 (34.0, 52.3), C-DC12 (27.9, 52.6), plus 0.5 mm): no bottom-side part.
edits.new:
C-DC11 (34.0, 52.3), C-DC12 (27.9, 52.6), plus 0.5 mm): no bottom-side part. (**superseded in r7:** the named keep-out
  retires; the bottom clearance rule below covers it.)
- **Bottom clearance rule (r7; replaces the r3 power-copper shadow (+1 mm) and the named bottom keep-out x 24.5-36.0,
  y 48.5-53.5).** Under the **bottom clearance rule** every CR bottom-side courtyard stays >= 1.0 mm in plan from every MB layer-1
  feature that is not GND (traces, pours and vias of any other net, measured on the copper rim including the polygon outline
  width) and from every MB part box. It applies on the footprint and on both tabs, and it is a superset of the shadow and of the
  keep-out (the five parts under the footprint are MB part boxes). The rule leaves 569.1 mm² of bottom area: footprint 391.6,
  tab X 44.3 and tab Y 133.2 mm², after the header bodies, the W1-W4 pads and the FT1/FT2 keep-outs (H.23(d); the foot
  keep-outs remove 34.6 mm², the 1.0 mm ring around the non-GND MB CHG header pads 4.1 mm²). The polyimide sheet stays as the
  second layer of the barrier. T-A-06 overlays the rule on the `.brd` layer-1 copper rims.
- **MB vias (r7, H.23(c2)):** the MB vias are **not tented**. All 368 vias carry the Eagle `alwaysstop` flag, and both stop-mask
  Gerbers (`soldermask_top.gbr`, `soldermask_bottom.gbr`) show a 0.9596 mm opening at every via. Under the CR the exposed via
  rings are covered by the polyimide sheet, and the bottom clearance rule keeps 1.0 mm from every non-GND via rim.
- **MB content under the tabs (r7, H.23(c)).** No MB part lies under either tab. Under tab X the MB layer 1 carries 29.16 mm² of
  non-GND copper, all logic nets: 3V3 3.41, CB-DISABLE 4.59, CHRG-STAT 4.52, CS-MDAC-FC 1.76, MPPT-DISABLE 4.63, SCL 5.11 and
  SDA 5.14 mm² (each +-0.3 mm², raster bias). Fifteen via pads overlap tab X; five are non-GND: 3V3 (56.431, 60.663), CS-MDAC-FC
  (58.420, 60.038), SCL (64.651, 58.809), CHRG-STAT (63.500, 58.928) and MPPT-DISABLE (65.024, 61.722), the last by its rim only.
  The rest is the board-wide GND pour. Under tab Y the MB carries only the GND pour: no non-GND copper and no via.
edits.note: bottom keep-out superseded; bottom clearance rule defined; vias not tented; MB content under the tabs

- Neighbours: CO-5V 0.1 mm right, LM1084 1.8 mm right (4.83 mm tall), J-NTC/J-BL left. CR parts are low-power (eFuse <= 0.17

edits.new:
- Neighbours: CO-5V 0.1 mm right, LM1084 1.8 mm right (4.83 mm tall), J-NTC/J-BL left. CR parts are low-power (eFuse <= 0.17
  W, H.14). (r7: these are the neighbours of the r6 rectangle; the tab neighbours are in the r7 trims bullet above.)
- **Thermal band (r7, H.23(h)).** The **thermal band** is the part of tab X within 6.4 mm of the MB 5V layer-1 copper rim
  around REG-5V (LM1084). Its boundary runs at y 60.5-62.34 across x 48.7-65.0, and it covers 84.9 of the 195.6 mm² of tab X
  (43 %). The band carries only pads, wires, the RTV bead and temperature-insensitive passives (R175, 1 % logic series resistors
  and pull-downs); no comparator, reference, 0.1 % divider, BAV199 or timing capacitor is placed in it. Row 1 of the tap field
  (low pad edges 2.233-4.190 mm from the rim), part of row 2 (4.773-7.808 mm) and part of the R175 courtyard (5.511-10.408 mm)
  lie in the band; rows 3-4 and the FT1 body (9.953-12.310 mm) lie outside it. The estimated MB surface rise is 4.5-23.5 C at
  1 mm, 3.3-17.0 C at 5 mm and 2.4-11.9 C at 10 mm from the rim (`round4/work/mb_mechanical.md` Table 4, ESTIMATE); MS4 replaces
  the estimate and confirms the split.
- **Far-end support feet (r7, H.23(i)).** Each tab carries a fitted foot by default: **FT1** under tab X near its tip and **FT2**
  under tab Y near its far edge. A foot body stays >= 0.5 mm inside the r7 outline, has no MB via pad of any net under it, and
  keeps >= 1.0 mm from every non-GND MB copper rim and every MB part box. FT1 is the largest bed area whose placement tolerance
  is >= +-0.25 mm in x and in y against that rule, at the exact max-min centre. FT2 is the 4 x 4 mm body at the largest lever
  from the pin-11 row (y 64.484) that keeps the same tolerance. The following table gives the adopted feet.

| Foot | Body (x by y), bed area | Centre | Body extent | Tolerance t (tx / ty) | Binding feature, nearest items | Keep-out (body + 0.5 mm) | Bed access |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FT1 | 4.0 x 1.6 mm, 6.40 mm² | (61.72, 66.705) | x 59.720-63.720, y 65.905-67.505 | 0.294 mm (0.304 / 0.294) | MPPT-DISABLE L1 trace (nearest non-GND rim 1.294 mm); nearest part box C-D2 3.64 mm; no via pad under the body | x 59.220-64.220, y 65.405-68.005 (5.0 x 2.6 mm) | RTV lane x 59.220-64.220, y 68.005-68.300 to the tab X top edge |
| FT2 | 4.0 x 4.0 mm, 16.00 mm² | (28.00, 73.250) | x 26.000-30.000, y 71.250-75.250 | 0.250 mm (7.060 / 0.250) | r7 outline edge (0.5 mm); no non-GND copper within 3 mm; nearest part box L-FC 1.76 mm; no via pad under the body; lever 8.766 mm from the pin-11 row | x 25.500-30.500, y 70.750-75.750 (5.0 x 5.0 mm) | 1.0 mm NPTH fill hole at the foot centre; no edge lane |

  The MB signal bundle (SDA, SCL, CHRG-STAT, MPPT-DISABLE, CB-DISABLE, 3V3, CS-MDAC-FC) crosses the whole tab X tip, so no
  4 x 4 mm FT1 meets the rule there. The next FT1 height, 4.0 x 1.7 mm, reaches only t 0.244 mm. A 4 x 4 mm FT1 at (62.50,
  61.40) over masked signal traces violates the rule (copper clearance -0.127 mm); it remains an operator option only, without
  the MB-mask fallback. FT2 alternative M, the mid-height spot (28.00, 71.320) with a lever of 6.836 mm and t 2.180 mm, is
  recorded but not adopted.
- **Foot construction and bedding (r7).** Each foot is a PA66 or PBT block of height h_f = 2.54 mm - t_bed = 2.24 mm at
  t_bed 0.30 mm (bed range 0.15-0.45 mm). It is bonded to the CR underside with neutral-cure RTV silicone before seating. The
  header bodies set the CR height, so the feet take no preload, and no wet adhesive is present while the 22 MB joints are
  soldered. After those joints are soldered and inspected, a neutral-cure RTV bed fills the 0.30 +- 0.15 mm gap between each
  foot and the polyimide sheet. FT1 is bedded with a syringe through its lane at the tab X top edge, before the W leads and the
  tap wires are fitted (PM4 order: 22 MB joints, inspection, FT1/FT2 beds, cure, then W1-W7 and the taps). The +y side of FT2
  lies behind the L-FC body, so FT2 is bedded through a 1.0 mm NPTH fill hole through tab Y and the foot at the foot centre
  (28.00, 73.250), injected from the CR top with a blunt needle. The hole lies 1.500 mm inside the foot body edge, and the CR top
  keeps a 2.0 mm copper and part keep-out disc around it (0.5 mm ring, 1.750 mm inside the r7 outline, booked in H.23(e)). Under
  the hole the MB carries GND pour under solder mask (nearest non-GND rim 7.18 mm, via pad 9.89 mm, part box 3.26 mm from the
  hole edge). Each bed cures >= 24 h before the T-A-09 bond check. Acetoxy-cure RTV is excluded (acetic acid near copper).
  TODO(verify: RTV datasheet: neutral cure, temperature rating, adhesion to polyimide without primer).
- **Foot removal and bond fallback (r7).** The polyimide sheet is the sacrificial layer: removal means cutting the bed and
  peeling the sheet, and in the baseline the MB solder mask is never bonded. If the T-A-09 bond check fails on polyimide, the
  sheet gets a cut-out at the foot spot and the bed bonds to the MB solder mask. The FT1 cut-out is no larger than its 5.0 x
  2.6 mm keep-out: it exposes no non-GND copper rim and no via pad, and the sheet still covers the MPPT-DISABLE trace by
  0.794 mm (H.23(i)). The FT2 cut-out is its 5.0 x 5.0 mm keep-out over GND pour only.
- **Tab stiffness and pin loads (r7, H.23(i); ORDER OF MAGNITUDE).** These figures assume a 20 GPa laminate, a clamped root and
  an RTV modulus of 1-3 MPa (ASSUMPTION, TODO(verify: RTV datasheet)); every resonance figure is an upper estimate, and MS5, MS6
  and T-F-18 decide. Tab X has a tip stiffness of 35.8 N/mm and 63.2 N/mm at the foot, against an RTV bed of 14-128 N/mm; its
  first mode is 1664-2353 Hz unpropped and 1924-3336 Hz propped (bed E 1-3 MPa, t 0.30 mm). Tab Y has 266.3 / 603.8 N/mm against
  a bed of 36-320 N/mm; its first mode is 4531-6407 Hz unpropped and 4726-7204 Hz propped. The worst header-pin load at 30 g is
  0.208-0.322 N without the feet and 0.168-0.297 N with them (r6 CR alone 0.067-0.134 N). A 10 N push at the tab X tip loads
  the worst pin with 2.69 N without FT1 and 0.52-1.99 N with it; at the tab Y tip the figures are 3.06 N and 1.64-2.83 N.
edits.note: thermal band, FT1/FT2 table, construction, fallback, stiffness/pin loads

- **EVM mount (r7).** The BQ25798EVM has no mounting holes: the corner circles are fiducials (SLUUCB5E Figs 4-1 to 4-4; BOM
  FID1-FID6; `round4/work/evm_geometry.md` section 3), and a hole drilled at a bumpon centre would cut the ground pour and 7-17
  stitching vias. The **EVM plate** is an insulating plate, fixed to the chassis, that carries the EVM and the EIB. The stock
  bumpons H1-H4 (3M SJ-5303, 11.18 mm diameter, 5.08 mm tall) stay fitted and rest on the plate. Two nylon clamp bars, or four
  corner L-clamps, with 0.5 mm silicone pads press edge lips of <= 2.0 mm; the clamps are notched at J8 and stay clear of
  TP48/TP49, the terminal wire faces and the fiducials. No fastener or adhesive bonds EVM copper to the plate, the CR or the
  chassis, and the EVM is not drilled. Plate and clamp geometry: TODO(design: from MS2 and MS7). J2 stays removed (EM7), and
  W1-W7 stay cable-tied to the chassis at 0.10 m intervals. T-A-02 checks the clamp fit and the insulation of the EVM copper
  (TP49, J1 pin 1) to the plate and the chassis (> 1 MOhm with W1-W7 disconnected).
- **EIB mount (r7).** The two M3 x 10 mm nylon standoffs stand on the EVM plate, so the EVM and the EIB form one rigid body and
  the E leads see no relative motion. The r6 placement rule (pad column 7 mm off the EVM right edge, E3 5 mm above TP33) is
  unchanged. At the reference placement the EIB bottom edge lies 4.84 mm from the J5 body top (>= 3 mm, H.23(l)). The E-lead
  build maxima follow A.5 (E1 90 mm, E5 65 mm; H.23(k)).
- **EVM reference placement (r7, H.23(l)).** The EVM plate sits on the chassis just past the MB +y edge (y 98.044). The EVM
  bottom edge faces the MB with a 20.0 mm gap for the J8 housing (J8 mates from -y; its pins end 13.76 mm short of the MB edge,
  which leaves room for the KK housing and the wire exit, TODO(verify: Molex 22-01-3047 mated length), MS2). The EVM right edge
  is at x 88.50, and the board rectangle is x -0.40-88.50, y 118.044-206.944 (0.40 mm past the MB -x edge). The right edge keeps
  4.97 mm from the Teensy 4.1 USB plug corridor (x 93.47-101.09 from y 93.73; 45.0 mm plug + bend, ASSUMPTION,
  TODO(measure: MS2)). The EIB, placed by the r6 rule, occupies x 93.50-117.50, y 159.65-195.65: it clears the assumed corridor
  by 20.92 mm but lies inside its x band, so a USB cable that runs straight +y for more than 65.9 mm would meet it. W3/W4 pass
  between the EVM right edge and the corridor in a 4.97 mm channel (pair outer size TODO(measure: MS2/MS7)). The chassis tie at
  the MB +y edge lies 29.744 mm from the tab X top edge (<= 30 mm, A.3). The W-lead route maxima for this placement are in A.3;
  until MS2 confirms the placement, the r6 0.30 m caps stay the T-A-02 bound.
- **USB corridor fallbacks (r7, H.23(l)).** For an open-ended corridor (x 93.47-101.09 from y 93.73, no end) three fallbacks
  were evaluated:
  - (i) the EVM + EIB group shifted -x by 27.03 mm (EVM x -27.43-61.47, EIB x 66.47-90.47, E leads unchanged) passes
    geometrically: no lead is blocked, every chassis tie is <= 30 mm, and the build maxima are W1 260, W2 270, W3 170, W4 170,
    W6 120, W7 SCL 180 and W7 SDA 170 mm, with W5 at 1.25 x route = 177 mm, all within 0.30 m. It needs 45.3 mm of chassis room
    past the MB -x edge (the W1 approach point at x -34.83 plus a 10.5 mm 20 AWG bend allowance, ASSUMPTION), clear of the
    J-BL/J-FC/J-NTC harness volume;
  - (ii) the EIB on the corridor +x side (EIB x 104.09-128.09) fails: the E-lead bundle and the shared EVM plate must span the
    corridor band, the W3/W4 J5 approach points (96.09, 142.24) and (96.09, 152.40) fall inside the corridor, W5 has no path on
    the +x side, and every E-lead maximum grows (E1 100 mm, E5 75 mm; E4 at 0.68 of its pickup-criterion limit);
  - (iii) the EIB at the EVM left edge fails: E4 (JP21 pin 1) needs a straight 82.3 mm against its 59 mm pickup-criterion limit.
  MS2 measures the chassis room and the USB plug + bend. The design adopts the reference placement, or fallback (i) when MS2
  shows that the corridor reaches the EIB or the W3/W4 channel. The "EVM rotated" variant is not evaluated (open item).

**r7 area booking (H.23(e); supersedes the H.18 / H.22(k) figures and the 95-103 % strict-basis overrun).** On the strict basis
of `round4/work/stackup_area.md`, the r7 outline offers 1081.1 mm² of usable top area (footprint 754.1, tab X 173.3, tab Y
153.7 mm², after the 3.14 mm² FT2 fill-hole keep-out disc) and 569.1 mm² of bottom area under the bottom clearance rule (A.7).
The adopted allocation moves R175 and the six 0.1 % divider resistors R109, R110, R111, R112, R114 and R115 (42.34 mm²) from the
r3 bottom set to the top; the comparator input filter capacitors C106, C107, C108 and C140 stay on the bottom. The dividers are
the high-impedance threshold nodes and belong beside the comparators, away from the MB copper; a filter capacitor is the
low-impedance end of its node. The following table lists the adopted case beside the sensitivity cases (H.23(e)).

| Case | Top mm² | Top U | Bottom mm² | Bottom U |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| r3 bottom set kept | 752.8 | 69.63 % | 435.2 | 76.48 % |
| r7 allocation, core (0.1 % dividers + filter capacitors) + R175 | 812.5 | 75.16 % | 375.5 | 65.99 % |
| r7 allocation, extended (core + reference, REF-3, FCC_ON and RGN_ON dividers and tap capacitors) + R175 | 864.7 | 79.98 % | 323.3 | 56.81 % |
| **r7 adopted** (R175 + R109, R110, R111, R112, R114, R115) | **795.1** | **73.55 %** | **392.9 of 569.1** | **69.04 %** |

The adopted case meets the <= 75 % target on both sides. A single-sided CR would need 101.8 % (all DNP footprints removed) to
109.9 % (all footprints) of the top area, so the CR stays double-sided. The comparators U102-U104, U115 and U119-U121 were
already top-side in the r3 booking; r7 moves their placement region to the footprint low-y band, not their side.
